messages:
Liz H: quick follow-up from the rfc thread — i'm worried our current metadata model mixes two orthogonal concerns: compatibility hints (what the runtime needs to know) and rollout semantics (how we schedule swaps).
Omar P: agreed. mixing them makes simple ops tasks like pin-for-customer become expensive.
Sasha M: can you sketch a concrete split?
Liz H: idea: keep a small, stable compatibility blob attached to a model tag (immutable), and keep rollout policy as separate resource that references tags + an ordered fallback vector. e.g.
```
model_tag: m-2026-05-fp16
compat_hints: ["min_ctx:2048","dtype:fp16","kv_shape:4x64"]
```
rollout_policy: { target: routeA, priority_list: [m-2026-05-fp16, m-2026-02-int8], canary_pct: 5 }
Kevin L: I like the separation. ops can update rollout_policy without touching model blobs. question: how do we guarantee the runtime honors 'compat_hints' when falling back? runtime needs cheap check.
Priya R: runtime check should be a bitset compare, not full schema validation — we can encode key hints into a small feature bitmask generated at model onboarding. fallback rule is then "model.bitmask & route.requirements == route.requirements". cheap and cacheable.
Omar P: edge case: model upgrades that are semantically breaking but pass bitmask (e.g., tokenizer change). we still need a higher-level fingerprint. maybe add a hash of the tokenizer + top-level schema into metadata so canary tools detect regressions.
Sasha M: if we add fingerprint, we also need clear upgrade semantics: soft-upgrade (auto-fallback allowed) vs hard-upgrade (requires manual pinning). include an enum in rollout_policy.
Liz H: tradeoffs: more metadata fields = more ops surface. but fewer fields = surprising fallbacks. i prefer explicit hard-upgrade for tokenizer or label-space changes.
Kevin L: how do we represent per-customer pins? keep them as overlays on top of rollout_policy (per-tenant override) or duplicate policy objects?
Priya R: overlay map is cleaner: route -> base_policy + tenant_overrides. we can store tenant overrides as small records referencing model_tag ids. rollout engine resolves overlays at request time and caches resolution for TTL. TTL should be short for dev velocity but long enough to avoid per-request DB lookups. 60s-300s range seems reasonable.
Omar P: folks, need to consider migration path for existing pinned models. we should generate bitmasks and fingerprints at onboarding and backfill; any model without fingerprint should be treated as hard-upgrade until validated.
Sasha M: last note: add a "compatibility_reason" human field in model blob so when a fallback happens ops get a clear message like: \"fallback blocked: tokenizer mismatch\" instead of opaque failures. small UX win.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for m-2026-05-fp16 -> routeA (5%) :rocket:
Liz H: great. next steps: i'll draft a minimal schema PR with bitmask spec + onboarding checks. tagging @Omar P for rollout engine changes and @Priya R for cache/TTL defaults. any objections?
Omar P: no objections. i'll take a pass on the engine impl notes.
Priya R: i'll propose TTL + cache invalidation hooks.
Sasha M: +1
Liz H: thanks everyone, i'll open the pr today and include backward compatibility plan for existing pins.
